title: PSC system reference: approving a held controlled renewal on Prescriptions & Renewals
content:
**Subject.** A renewal of a controlled prescription of the Prescriptions & Renewals line that was placed on hold may be approved from hold, granting the renewal's fills.

**Formal clauses.**

1. Completing the missing requirement lets the held renewal be approved from hold, and every other requirement of the class must still be current on the renewal date.

2. For a class whose renewals need the prescriber's own signature, that review is the one that placed the renewal on hold naming its single missing requirement, so the approval from hold is recorded without a second signature once that requirement is complete.

3. A controlled renewal's fills are not fixed until the prescription shows a controlled-substance agreement the patient signed within the class's agreement renewal months before the renewal date.

3.1 Equivalently: while the agreement signature date shown on the prescription is older than the class's agreement renewal months before the renewal date, or no signature date is shown, the number of fills of the controlled renewal is not yet fixed.

### Situation of use and capability

The tool approves a pending or held renewal of a prescription and grants its new fills. One call makes the prescription active again with today as its renewal date, a new last date to fill of today plus the class's validity period (today counted as day one), and no hold; any fills left on the old authorization are voided as `superseded_by_renewal`, and one new fill authorization with reason renewal is posted for the given number of fills at the prescription's current per-fill days' supply, which become the fills it still authorizes.

### How it is invoked

The tool is `approve_prescription_renewal_192bec69`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `prescription_id` | reference number of the prescription whose renewal is approved, as shown by the prescription lookup for this patient | identifier |
| `appointment_id` | reference number of the patient's completed visit with the prescribing department that keeps the visit requirement current, as shown by the appointment lookup for this patient | identifier |
| `fills` | number of fills the renewal authorizes, the initial fill included; it also becomes the fills the prescription still authorizes | whole number written as an integer greater than 0 |

The tool has no enumerated parameters.

### Return

On success the receipt is a dictionary: `rx_event_id` (reference of the new renewal authorization entry), `prescription_id`, `appointment_id` (the qualifying visit), `fills` (integer fills granted), `days_supply_per_fill` (integer days per fill), `voided_fills` (integer fills voided from the old authorization, 0 when none), `renewed_date` (today, YYYY-MM-DD), `expiration_date` (new last date to fill, YYYY-MM-DD) and `status`, which reads "active" when the renewal is approved. Afterwards the prescription lookup shows it active with the new dates and fills, and the fill history shows the void, where there was one, and the renewal authorization. No other return or error is defined for the tool.

### Reading clauses 1 and 2 (hypothetical)

A Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription was placed on hold by its prescriber for a missing drug screen. Once a resulted screen is recorded, the renewal may be approved from hold without a second prescriber signature, provided the visit, agreement and database-check requirements are also current on the renewal date.
